note: Decision trees of the Tense & Mood Lab (spec 06 E7, spec 08 §4). A result names card or contrast card ids and may give the answer word, why it fits and an example.

trees.title: ser or estar?
trees.intro: Think of the sentence you want to say with “to be”. A few questions lead to the right verb, and sometimes it is neither of the two.

start.question: What does “to be” tell us in your sentence?

options.label: Where a person or a thing is
options.why: Location takes estar, even for places that never move.

example.text: Mi oficina está cerca de la estación.
example.en: My office is near the station.

options.label: Where an event happens: a party, a class, a concert
options.why: Events take ser, also for where they happen.

example.text: La clase es en el aula 3.

options.label: Who someone is, their job, or where they are from
options.why: Identity, jobs and origin take ser.

example.text: Soy Diego, soy de Quito y soy cocinero.
example.en: I'm Diego, I'm from Quito and I'm a cook.

options.label: The time, the day or the date
options.why: The time and dates take ser.

options.label: How old someone is
options.why: Spanish does not use “to be” for age. Age takes tener.

options.label: What someone is doing right now (“is doing”)
options.why: An action in progress takes estar + gerund, never ser.

options.label: What a thing is made of
options.why: Material is part of what something is: ser de.

example.en: The table is made of wood.

options.label: What someone or something is like, or how they are

describe.question: Is it what they are like in general, or how they are at the moment?
describe.help: Would you say it to describe them to someone who has never met them, or about today?

options.label: What they are like in general: personality, looks, size, color

example.text: Mi abuelo es alto y muy tranquilo.
example.en: My grandfather is tall and very calm.

options.label: How they feel or how they are right now: tired, glad, ill, busy
options.why: Feelings and states at the moment take estar.

options.label: Just “How are you?” or “I'm fine”
options.why: Bien and mal go with estar.

example.en: How is your father? —He's fine, thanks.

trees.title: Pick the past tense
trees.intro: You want to say something about the past. A few questions lead to the indefinido, the imperfecto or the perfecto.

start.question: Do you say when it happened?
start.help: Look for a time word in your sentence.

options.label: Yes, a finished time: ayer, anoche, el año pasado, en 2019, hace dos años
Yes, a time that is not over yet: hoy, esta mañana, esta semana
options.why: In Spain a time that is not over takes the perfecto; in most of Latin America the indefinido is normal.

example.text: Hoy he trabajado mucho. / Hoy trabajé mucho.

options.label: No, it is about my life up to now: ever, never, already, not yet
options.answer: perfecto (much of Latin America: also indefinido with ya / todavía no)
options.why: Experiences and things done or not done yet, with no time given, take the perfecto. In many Latin American countries ya and todavía no also go with the indefinido: ¿Ya comiste?

example.en: Have you ever been to Peru?

options.label: No, it is a description or a habit: as a child, before, always

finished.question: Within that finished time, is it an event or the scene?
finished.help: An event moves the story on. The scene is what things were like or what was going on.

options.label: An event: something happened, once or a counted number of times
options.why: A finished event at a finished time takes the indefinido.

example.text: Ayer fui al cine con Diego.
example.en: Yesterday I went to the movies with Diego.

options.label: A closed period: three years, all day, two weeks
options.why: A period with a clear end counts as one event.

example.en: I was in Peru for two weeks.

options.label: The scene: the weather, the time, how someone felt, what was going on
options.why: The background of a story takes the imperfecto, even inside a finished time.

example.en: Last night it was cold and raining.

options.label: What used to happen again and again

example.text: De niño jugaba en la calle.
example.en: As a child I used to play in the street.

options.label: What someone or something was like, age or the time
options.why: Descriptions, age and the time in the past take the imperfecto.

example.text: Mi abuela era muy alta y tenía el pelo blanco.
example.en: My grandmother was very tall and had white hair.

options.label: An action in progress when something else happened
options.why: The action in progress takes the imperfecto; the event that interrupts it takes the indefinido.

example.en: I was sleeping when the phone rang.
